title: Knowledge check: Testing Router and Pinia

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Testing Router and Pinia”?
options: Test only private implementation details and ignore user-visible behavior.
Rely on one screenshot as proof of every application state.
Make end-to-end tests the only test level.
Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Testing Router and Pinia directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Mocking or configuring router instances”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Rely on one screenshot as proof of every application state.
Make end-to-end tests the only test level.
Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
Test only private implementation details and ignore user-visible behavior.
questions.answer_key: Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Mocking or configuring router instances”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Testing Router and Pinia” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
